artboards.title: The sidebar, with a way in

annotations.text:
Adding a project is not hard — it is hidden.

Two real faults, found in the code rather than guessed at:

1. The Explorer's + says it adds "a project, topic or anything else" and always makes a folder.

2. "Add project…" exists, but only on a solution's right-click menu. From the Develtech workspace there is no way in at all.

So this keeps the sidebar exactly as it is and gives adding a front door. Static mockups, in the app's own tokens.

Four kinds, named in the words you would use rather than the app's: a code project here, a code project from GitHub, an area with no code, a folder inside a project.

Two of them need a second step — a folder to point at, or a repository to clone. The other two are one field and Enter.

One thing is deliberately absent: "new empty repository". An app that quietly runs git init in your folders is one you stop trusting. Easy to add if you want it.

Four ways in, all opening the same picker, none of them removing anything that is there now.

The sidebar you called complex is untouched on purpose: making adding obvious and simplifying the tree are two jobs, and doing both at once leaves you unable to tell which one helped.
